name: Louisiana
summary: Statutes: legis.la.gov serves every law as a small Law.aspx?d={id} page (unofficial per its disclaimer). The five codes (Civil, Civil Procedure, Criminal Procedure, Evidence, Children's) have GET table-of-contents pages that map article → id, but the Revised Statutes and Constitution TOCs are POST-only, so R.S. ids must be found by web search or read from Justia (constructible, 2025 edition, WebFetch only). Court rules: the Uniform Rules of the Courts of Appeal are an official PDF on fifthcircuit.org; Supreme Court and District Court rules sit on lasc.org, a Blazor app neither tool can read. Admin code: the official LAC and Register are .docx only (unreadable); Cornell LII has a constructible per-section LAC. Case law: lasc.org is unreadable, so Supreme Court opinions come from Justia (court news-release PDFs on cases.justia.com, script-readable); the Second Circuit has GET year listings (2009–), the Fifth Circuit lists recent PDFs, and the First, Third and Fourth Circuits need JavaScript or POST — use Justia. Writ dispositions (subsequent history) have no readable free source.

citation_map.notes: Civil-law jurisdiction: the Civil Code, Code of Civil Procedure, Code of Criminal Procedure, Code of Evidence and Children's Code are cited by ARTICLE ('art.'), never by section; the Revised Statutes are cited title:section ('La. R.S. 9:2800', no § in Louisiana style; Bluebook 'La. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 9:2800'). law_aliases map each code abbreviation to the legis.la.gov TOC folder key. GUARD: Texas, California and other states also have a 'Civil Code', 'Code of Civil Procedure' and 'Code of Criminal Procedure' (Texas cites 'art.' too); bare 'Civil Code article', 'C.C.P. art.', 'Code of Criminal Procedure article', 'C.E. art.' and bare 'R.S. 9:2800' are context_required and route here only with a Louisiana marker (La./LSA-/Louisiana/'(La.' court parenthetical) elsewhere in the query. Louisiana has used a public-domain/vendor-neutral form since 1994 (La. Sup. Ct. Gen. Admin. Rules Part G § 8, from memory): docket number + court + exact date in parentheses, e.g. '2022-K-01824 (La. 12/8/23)', '2022-32 (La. App. 5 Cir. 11/16/22)', '56,618 (La. App. 2 Cir. …)'; the '(La.' / '(La. App. N Cir.' parenthetical is what makes it distinctive. Docket formats differ by court: Supreme Court YYYY-TT-NNNNN (older YYYY-NNNN); 1st Cir. YYYY CA/CW/KA NNNN; 2nd Cir. NN,NNN-CA; 3rd Cir. YY-NNN; 4th Cir. YYYY-CA-NNNN; 5th Cir. YY-CA-NNN. Bare dockets, bare So. 2d/So. 3d (Southern Reporter is shared with AL, FL, MS) and bare 'writ denied' are context_required. Subsequent history in Louisiana is almost always a Supreme Court WRIT disposition ('writ denied, 2021-01234 (La. 1/12/22), 330 So. 3d 1234'), not 'review denied'/'cert. denied'. Court rules: Supreme Court Rules use Roman numerals (Rule X, § 5); District Court Rules decimals (9.5); Uniform Rules of the Courts of Appeal 'N-N.N' (2-18.1). LAC citations use title:part(Roman).section ('LAC 33:III.501'); the Louisiana Register is cited 'LR vol:page'. CourtListener ids are from memory and unverified; CourtListener uses one id ('lactapp') for all five circuits, so filter by circuit in the parenthetical.

sources.title: Louisiana Laws — Civil Code, Code of Civil Procedure, Code of Criminal Procedure, Code of Evidence, Children's Code (legis.la.gov)
sources.official_status_evidence: LawSearch.aspx 'Disclaimer': provisions 'have not been edited for publication and are not official or authoritative' (https://legis.la.gov/legis/LawSearch.aspx).
sources.coverage: Current text of the five codes, one article per Law.aspx page, with amendment history (Acts) at the foot.

access.pattern_rules: doc_id is an internal numeric document id, NOT derivable from the article number (CC 2315 → 109369, CC 1 → 108528, CE 702 → 72506, CCP 966 → 112309, C.Cr.P. 894 → 112888, Ch.C. 101 → 72534). Each code has one GET table-of-contents page listing every article with its Law.aspx?d= link, labelled '{KEY} {article}' (e.g. 'CC 2315', 'CCP 966', 'CCRP 894', 'CE 702', 'CHC 101'). TOC folder ids: CC=67, CCP=68, CCRP=69, CE=70, CHC=71 (also CONST=72 and RS=75 — but those two TOCs are ASP.NET postback-only; see la-rs-legis / la-const-legis). LawPrint.aspx?d={doc_id} is a print view with the same body.
access.navigation: Laws_Toc.aspx?folder={67|68|69|70|71}&level=Parent → link whose text is exactly '{KEY} {article}' (fetch_doc.py links URL '^CC 2315$' --regex) → Law.aspx?d={id} holds the article body. The Civil Code TOC is one ~867K-character page (5,034 links): use fetch_doc.py links with a filter, not the fetch tool.

automation.notes: Law.aspx pages are small (1.6–10K chars) so neither tool truncates. The Civil Code TOC (~867K chars) far exceeds the fetch tool's window; resolve article→id with the script. WebFetch was tested only on a search-result URL (it worked); built Law.aspx URLs may need per-URL approval, so the script is primary. legis.la.gov and www.legis.la.gov serve the same pages; 'Legis'/'legis' path case is ignored.

access.pattern_rules: doc_id is an internal numeric id not derivable from title:section (9:2800 → 107250, 9:2800.16 → 408378, 9:1590 → 106718, 9:229 → 107045). Page heading reads 'RS {title}:{section}'. The RS title TOC (folder=75) and the 'View a Specific Law' box on LawSearch.aspx (law body RS + Title + Section) are ASP.NET POST postbacks — no GET URL reaches a section. Justia's 2006 edition uses the same ids (law.justia.com/codes/louisiana/2006/123/107250.html = RS 9:2800) but only for sections that existed in 2006.
access.navigation: Find the id with a web search for the page heading: site:legis.la.gov "RS 9:2800" (exact heading form 'RS {title}:{section}'), or the section catchline + 'Law.aspx'; confirm the 'RS t:s' heading on the fetched page. If no id is found, use la-codes-justia (constructible) instead. Never guess ids.

automation.notes: Search-result Law.aspx URLs pass the fetch tool; built ones may be gated, so prefer the script. A bare site: search for 'RS 9:2800' returned wrong sections; adding the catchline found it.
